# Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES (AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66)

## Problem statement

The dedicated `GymCentipede` enemy gym scene is discovered by the generic `Gym<Name>`
glob in `GymIndex` and rendered in the left-hand **plain scenes** column. The
Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it belongs in the middle **ENEMIES** column —
exactly where the analogous `GymBoss` scene already lives — so the index no longer
miscategorises an enemy testbed as a general-purpose scene.

## Users

- **Developer browsing the gym index** — expects enemy gym scenes to be grouped in the
  ENEMIES column so an enemy testbed is launched from the correct section.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear in the **ENEMIES** column so that
  every enemy testbed is grouped together on the index.
- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear exactly once on the index (in the
  ENEMIES column, not the plain-scene column) so I don't see a confusing, miscategorised
  entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `GymCentipede` removed from the plain scenes column:** `GymIndex.listedScenes`
      no longer contains `GymCentipede` and no `Centipede` text row is rendered at the
      plain-scenes column X (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.scenes`).
- [ ] **AC2 — No separate `Centipede` entry on the gym index:** `GymIndex.listedEnemyScenes`
      contains exactly `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]` — no dedicated `Centipede` row — and
      `GymCentipede` is not listed in any index column (per the producer's review decision:
      "it should appear in the dropdown in the enemies gym", not as a separate entry).
- [ ] **AC3 — The `Centipede` enemy type appears in the in-panel dropdown of the enemies
      gym:** `GymFodderEnemies`'s enemy selector (`enemy-gym-select`) lists a `Centipede`
      option (label `Centipede`), alongside the discovered non-boss `EnemyConfig`s, and
      seeding `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })` works.
- [ ] **AC4 — Selecting `Centipede` in the enemies gym runs the shared linked chain:** the
      scene rebuilds via the *same* `CentipedeChain` / `Centipede` code `PlayScene` and
      `GymCentipede` run (`src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts`): one `Centipede`
      segment per `CENTIPEDE_SEGMENT_COUNT`, a shared chain, and the config-tuning controls
      hidden (the Centipede has no CSV row to tune or save). Switching back to a config
      archetype restores the config-driven formation and the tuning controls.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** `GymIndex.test.ts` drops the dedicated-row expectations; new
      assertions cover the dropdown `Centipede` option (presence, label, chain build,
      control hiding, round-trip back to a config). Every existing test continues to pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
      comments, `README.md`, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the three-column layout and the existing column X positions (`GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`)
  unchanged; this is a categorisation change only.
- Mirror the existing `GymBoss` exclusion/surfacing pattern in `GymIndex.ts`; do **not**
  introduce a new generic "auto-route every enemy gym to ENEMIES" mechanism (scope creep —
  see Risks).
- No behavioural change to `GymCentipede` itself (only its index visibility/labelling).
- Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — it stays a pure discovery helper; the
  column categorisation is owned by `GymIndex`.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds `this.entries` from
  `discoverGymScenes(loadGymSceneModules())`, filtering out `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`
  and the Dev Utilities set (`DEV_UTILITY_SCENE_KEYS`). `GymCentipede` is **not** filtered,
  so it falls through into the left plain-scenes column.
- `this.enemyEntries` is currently hard-coded to `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.test.ts` asserts chain parity only; it does not assert index
  listing, so it needs no change.
- The Centipede is a **wave opt-in** (`centipede: true` in `PlayScene`), not a CSV enemy
  config, so it is not part of the `GymFodderEnemies` dropdown roster.

## Desired change (revised per producer review)

The producer's manual review (2026-10-14) rejected the dedicated-ENEMIES-row approach:
*"It appears in the enemies column now, but as a separate entry, it should appear in the
dropdown in the enemies gym."* The Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it should be
selectable **inside** the reusable enemies gym (`GymFodderEnemies`) rather than occupying a
separate index row (and it must stay out of the plain-scenes column).

1. Keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain-scenes list in `GymIndex.ts`.
2. Remove the dedicated `Centipede` ENEMIES row (`this.enemyEntries` reverts to
   `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`).
3. Surface the Centipede as a dedicated option in `GymFodderEnemies`'s in-panel enemy
   selector (`enemy-gym-select`): selecting it (or deep-linking
   `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })`) swaps the scene to the **shared** centipede chain
   formation. The chain code is owned once in
   `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` and consumed by both `GymCentipede` and
   `GymFodderEnemies`, so game/gym parity holds by construction.
4. While the Centipede is active, hide the config-tuning controls (`#enemy-gym-config-body`):
   it is a wave opt-in, not a CSV row, so there is nothing to tune or save.
5. Update the module/class doc comments that enumerate the column exclusions, README and
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`
   (pure discovery helper) or add a generic auto-route mechanism for every enemy scene.

## Key Files
## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` — (new) the single shared Centipede chain
  formation config + per-scene chain registry, consumed by `GymCentipede` and
  `GymFodderEnemies`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.ts` — thin wrapper over the shared module (unchanged public
  API).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — add the `Centipede` option to the enemy selector;
  branch `init`/`_selectEnemy` to the shared centipede formation; hide `#enemy-gym-config-body`
  while the Centipede is active.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain scenes; remove the
  dedicated ENEMIES row; update column doc comments.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — updated and
  new assertions as per AC5.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §Gym surface / §8.5: record that the Centipede
  is surfaced in the enemies-gym dropdown, excluded from the plain scene list and not a
  separate ENEMIES row.
- `README.md` — §Gym Index Entry Scene: ENEMIES column roster is `Fodder Enemies`, `Boss`;
  the Centipede lives in the fodder gym's dropdown.

## Related work
## Related work

- **Boss appears in both lists on index screen (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X)** — established the
  precedent: exclude an enemy scene from the plain-scene column and surface a dedicated
  ENEMIES row that boots the scene directly.
- **Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E)** —
  defines the three-column index layout and the ENEMIES column semantics.
- **Centipede segmented chain (AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86)** — created the `GymCentipede` scene.
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** —
  sibling categorisation pattern (Dev Utilities column owns tooling scenes).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MV2XDEKN0031KX4** – Test: gym parity intact (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: archetype, centipede, column, gym, scene (+34 more)
- `README.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, enemies (+33 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, currently (+30 more)

Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (revised by producer review):** "should be an enemy" means the Centipede
  should be reachable **inside** the enemies gym — surfaced as a dedicated **option in the
  `GymFodderEnemies` in-panel enemy selector**, which boots the same shared linked-chain code
  — rather than as a separate index entry *or* a CSV fodder config (the Centipede is a wave
  opt-in, not a CSV row). The producer rejected the dedicated ENEMIES row in review
  (2026-10-14).
- **Risk: Low.** A categorisation + dropdown-surface change with shared-code extraction; no
  gameplay, entity or spawn behaviour changes. The dedicated `GymCentipede` scene is
  unchanged in behaviour and keeps its parity tests.
- **Failure mode:** a `Centipede` label present on the index at all would make the
  `findTextAt` label lookups ambiguous — resolved by keeping `GymCentipede` out of every
  index column; it is only reachable through the fodder gym's dropdown.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "auto-route every enemy gym scene to the ENEMIES column"
  mechanism is out of scope here; if wanted it should be captured as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** Research summary: the seed intent, combined
  with the existing `GymBoss` precedent (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X) and the documented three-column
  index contract (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §"Gym surface", `README.md` §"Gym Index Entry Scene"), was sufficient to draft a clear
  brief. The one interpretation choice (dedicated ENEMIES **scene** row that boots
  `GymCentipede` directly, rather than adding a fodder-dropdown config) is recorded as an
  explicit documented assumption under Risks & assumptions.

# Intake brief — Smart Bomb is too powerful

## Problem statement

The Smart Bomb power-up (Defender homage, AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ) is too strong: a hold-full reward makes its screen-wide pulse repeat every **5 seconds** at base level (and up to every 2 s at the cap), and its pulse radius (1200 → 2400 px) already exceeds the whole 960×540 play field from the first pickup. The result is a near-continuous screen clear that trivialises every wave the moment the permanent smart bomb is earned.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the smart bomb to stay a tense "panic button" (rare, high-value wake-up) rather than a passive auto-win.

**User story:** "As a player who earned the permanent smart bomb from the hold-full choice, I want it to pulse rarely (once every ~30 seconds at first, never more often than once per 10 seconds) and to cover only a modest area around my ship, so the game stays challenging instead of auto-playing."

## Desired change

1. **Pulse rate (permanent smart bomb only):** fire every `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds — 30 s on the first grant (level 0), −2 s per further level, floor 10 s. A field pickup (one-shot) still fires exactly once on collection.
2. **Pulse radius (both permanent and runtime-collected):** base = **200 px** (10 × `SHIP_SIZE` = 10 × 20), additive **+2 % of base per level** → `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))`, capped at 400 px (2× base). No longer screen-wide.
3. **Damage unchanged:** stays 1 → 3 HP per pulse (no change).
4. Resolved through the same shared `AoEDescriptor`/`screenPulse` seam so the game and every gym run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A permanent smart bomb pulses on the interval `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` seconds: 30 s at level 0 (first grant), 28 s at level 1, … 10 s at level 10 and beyond; `smartBombInterval()` reflects this schedule.
- The smart bomb pulse radius resolves to `min(400, 200 × (1 + 0.02 × level))` px: 200 px base (10× ship size), additive +2 % of base per level, capped at 400 px. Applies to both permanent pulses and one-shot field pickups.
- Smart bomb damage per pulse is unchanged (1 → 3 HP across levels).
- Behaviour lands in the shared core (`effects.ts` / `powerUpLevels.ts` + the AoE seam) so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes (`GymPowerUpsCombat` and the shared `powerUpLeveling.parity` tests) run identical code — no divergent copies.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, "screen-wide" descriptions of the pulse must be corrected in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` (§6).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (including updated `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `effects.test.ts` and `AoeWeapons.test.ts` assertions that pin the old 1200/2400 px and 0.2→0.5/s values).

## Constraints

- The level model in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` currently stores every variable on the `exponential-saturation` curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`; the `UpgradeCurve` union has a single member). The two new schedules — linear-descending interval and linear-additive radius — are **not expressible** by that curve, so a new curve type (e.g. a linear/clamped variant) must be added to `src/utils/curve.ts` and consumed by the smart-bomb specs. Keep the resolver pure, deterministic, monotonic and clamped as today.
- The pulse-frequency axis is stored non-decreasing (`smartBombFrequency`, pulses/s); the desired *interval* schedule is descending, so represent the change as `frequency = 1 / max(10, 30 − 2×level)` (non-decreasing, meets the model's monotonicity contract) or restructure the variable — implementation choice, but `smartBombInterval()` must return the documented schedule.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): the change must be applied once in the shared core and consumed by both sides; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` enforces this.
- `SHIP_SIZE = 20` (`src/core/constants.ts`) is the ship-size base used by the magnet convention (`magnetRadius`), and 10× of it = **200 px** (operator decision Q1-A).

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.smart_bomb`: `aoeRadius` base 1200/cap 2400 (k=0.3, exponential-saturation), `smartBombDamage` base 1/cap 3, `smartBombFrequency` base 0.2/cap 0.5 (k=0.3).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `isSmartBombPermanent()`, `smartBombFrequency()`, `smartBombInterval()`, `smartBombAoe()`, `updateSmartBomb(dt)`; permanent pulse timer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_updateSmartBomb(dt)` consumes `smartBombAoe()` and applies it through the shared AoE seam; `CombatScene.onSmartBombPulse`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `SHIP_SIZE = 20`.
- Tests pinning current values: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` (102–107, 136–163), `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (~596–656), `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts` (~810–866).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/curve.ts` — new linear/clamped curve type (currently only `exponential-saturation`).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — re-spec the three smart-bomb variables (radius schedule, frequency/interval schedule; damage unchanged) with the new curve.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `smartBombInterval()` / `smartBombAoe()` resolve the new schedules; comments updated.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — only if the seam needs adjustment (expected: none).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a named constant for the 10× ship-size / 2 % tuning knobs.
- Tests: `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`.

## Related work

- AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ — Defender smart bomb pulse (the original feature being re-balanced; completed).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — Design level curves for all power-ups (the model this change extends).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — gym↔game parity convention (must be preserved).
- AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4 — Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (adjacent pickup behaviour; completed).
- AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4 / AH-0MV1BIUGE005BJO8 — classic power-up research epics that introduced the smart bomb (background).

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MV1BIWP9003EHRQ** – Defender smart bomb pulse (completed)
- **AH-0MTVYCM2N002NKE4** – Player pickup pickups as soon as they touch (completed)
- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** – Design level curves for all power-ups (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `README.md`
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Curve-family extension risk:** adding a linear/clamped curve to `src/utils/curve.ts` touches shared machinery used by all levelled variables — the new curve must stay pure/deterministic and unit-tested so it cannot regress weapon or other power-up curves. Mitigation: new curve type is additive; existing specs keep `exponential-saturation`; parity/equivalence tests guard the seam.
- **Value-inversion risk:** switching the smart-bomb axis meaning (interval vs frequency) could break `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` / hold-full overlay deltas or the monotonicity contract — keep frequency non-decreasing (`1/interval`) and clamp, and pin expected resolved values in `powerUpLevels.test.ts`.
- **Scope creep:** opportunities observed during implementation (e.g. retuning the *Bomb* power-up, smart bomb visual redesign for a smaller radius) must be recorded as linked work items, not absorbed into this item.

## Assumptions

- "lvl1" in the request maps to **level 0** (first collection) in the code's level semantics — i.e. the base schedule is 30 s and the basic radius is 200 px at first pickup.
- Interval applies only to the *permanent* (hold-full) smart bomb; the one-shot field pickup fires once regardless.
- Damage tuning (1 → 3) is out of scope for this change.
- Radius cap of 2× base (400 px) is acceptable (operator decision Q2-A); radius growth is **additive** (+2 % of base per level).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "10× the radius of the ship: what is the base radius?" — Answer (operator): **A — 10 × SHIP_SIZE = 200 px**, matching the magnet/scoop "× ship size" convention (`magnetRadius` uses `shipSize` as the base unit). Source: interactive reply to intake round 1. Research: `src/core/constants.ts` `SHIP_SIZE = 20`; `src/powerups/effects.ts` `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)`.
- Q2: "2 % every lvl: additive or compound, and cap?" — Answer (operator): **A — additive** `base × (1 + 0.02 × level)`, **cap 2× base = 400 px**. Source: interactive reply. Research: current `powerUpLevels.ts` variables are monotonic non-decreasing with infinite level space, so a finite cap is required by the model's clamping contract.
- Q3: "Confirm interval schedule `max(10, 30 − 2×level)` with level 0 = first pickup, and damage unchanged?" — Answer (operator): **Confirmed.** Source: interactive reply. Research: `effects.ts` `updateSmartBomb`/`smartBombInterval` (permanent only); field pickup path is one-shot.

# Distributed versions of the game do not use the correct Bot definitions

**Priority:** critical · **Issue type:** bug · **Stage:** intake

## Problem statement

Bot-tuning definitions live **only** in `window.localStorage` (key
`ai-hell-bot-tuning`, written by `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`), and the
shipped **Watch Demo** / attract mode (`PlayScene` demo mode) reads that store
when a demo starts. `localStorage` is per-browser, per-origin and per-machine —
it is not part of the repository or of a build. When the code is checked out on
another machine, or served from a distributed build (e.g. the GitHub Pages
alpha), a fresh browser has no saved state and every demo silently falls back
to the built-in `Default` config instead of the tuned Bot definitions the
developer has in their build environment. The enemy/ship/difficulty CSVs do
ship with the build (bundled via `?raw` in `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`); bot
tuning has no equivalent, which is why only bot behaviour is affected.

**Goal:** a Git-tracked bot-tuning configuration is bundled into every build as
the baseline, so distributed builds and fresh machines fly the correct Bot
definitions, while a local user's saved `localStorage` selection still wins
locally.

## Users

- **Developer / designer of the demo bot:** tunes named configurations in the
  Bot Tuning gym, and expects every build of the game — including one checked
  out or served on another machine — to fly those definitions rather than the
  generic factory defaults.
- **Producer / release reviewer:** runs demos and records gameplay video
  (`npm run capture`, `npm run record -- --bot`) from any checkout and expects
  the footage to show the tuned bot, not a default fallback.

Example user stories:

- *As a developer tuning the demo bot, I want the tuned configuration committed
  to the repo so that a fresh checkout, build and demo run plays my tuning
  without re-exporting anything.*
- *As a producer, I want the GitHub Pages alpha to show the correct bot
  behaviour so release footage and preview builds match the tuned design.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Bundled baseline ships and is used.** A Git-tracked bot-tuning configuration file (the exact exported store shape `{ version, current, configs }`) is committed and bundled into dev and production builds; in a browser with no (or corrupt/missing) `localStorage` state, `loadBotTuningState()` returns the bundled configuration set and the shipped demo (`PlayScene` demo mode) flies it.
- **AC2 — Local overrides are preserved.** When `localStorage` holds a saved state, the currently-selected local configuration wins locally — precedence is `localStorage` → bundled baseline, mirroring the CSV config pattern; a fresh browser shows the bundled baseline, not factory defaults.
- **AC3 — Corrupt-safe, unchanged fallback behaviour.** Missing/invalid `localStorage` (and an unreadable/invalid bundled file) never crashes or degrades demo behaviour; the store remains versioned and corrupt-safe.
- **AC4 — Refresh workflow round-trips.** The bundled file is byte-equivalent to the Bot Tuning gym's **Export** output (via `serialiseBotTuningState()`), so *tune → Export → commit → build → fresh browser* reproduces the tuned demo; the workflow is documented.
- **AC5 — Recording tools see the baseline.** `npm run capture` (demo path) and `npm run record -- --bot` launched without `--bot-config` in a fresh Chromium now record the bundled baseline (previously factory defaults); passing `--bot-config` still overrides for a specific clip.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit and integration tests cover the fallback and precedence; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass; the gym↔game duplicate-body parity guard stays green.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §12).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No changes to bot *decision* code — only which tunables construct the
  brain/governor (consistent with AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL non-goals).
- The store's persistence model stays `localStorage`; the bundled file is a
  baseline fallback, not a new write path.
- The shipped file must be **Git-tracked** (never git-ignored).
- Normal (human) Play Game sessions stay untouched — the bot seam remains
  inert outside demo mode.
- No schema/version bump is expected (`BOT_TUNING_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` shape is
  reused).

## Existing state

- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — `createDefaultState()` seeds only the built-in
  `Default` config; `parseState()` already validates the exact exported
  `{ version, current, configs }` shape and is corruption-safe, so a bundled
  JSON blob can reuse it.
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — the established bundling point for Git-tracked
  design data (`?raw` CSV imports consumed by production/static builds).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — demo mode already calls
  `getCurrentBotTuningConfig()` on start and rebuilds the brain/governor
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL); no change needed there.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` / `scripts/record-session.mjs` — launch a
  fresh Chromium; inject `--bot-config` only when the flag is passed.
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (§ Bot-tuning configuration),
  `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`, `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` (§12).

## Desired change

1. **Add the shipped baseline.** Commit a new `src/data/bot-tuning.json` holding
   the exported store state (produced via the gym's **Export** button /
   `serialiseBotTuningState()` from the developer's build environment) and
   export it from `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` (JSON import or a `?raw` parse,
   matching how the CSVs bundle).
2. **Make it the fallback.** In `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`,
   `createDefaultState()` / `parseState()` no longer default to the lone
   factory `Default` when storage is empty; instead the bundled file is parsed
   through the existing `parseState()` validation (which already falls back
   safely on malformed input) so a fresh browser seeds the bundled
   configurations — keeping a `Default`-named entry that carries the shipped
   values so the gym selector and config-name reporting are unchanged.
   Precedence stays `localStorage` → bundled baseline.
3. **Docs.** Document the baseline, the precedence rule, and the refresh
   workflow (tune → Export → overwrite `src/data/bot-tuning.json` → commit).
4. **Tests.** Add store tests (no storage / corrupt storage / invalid bundled
   file → bundled baseline; saved storage wins), a demo-mode test asserting the
   demo flies the bundled baseline in a fresh profile, and keep capture-script
   tests green.

## Key Files

- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — **new**, Git-tracked baseline (exported store
  shape).
- `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — export the bundled bot-tuning baseline.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` — seed from the bundled baseline when storage is
  empty/invalid.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.test.ts` — new baseline/precedence cases.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / demo-mode integration test — verify the fresh
  profile demo flies the bundled baseline.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — unchanged code; verify fresh-browser capture
  uses the baseline (test/doc only).
- Docs: `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`,
  `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`.

## Related work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "the correct Bot definitions" are the Bot Tuning gym's named
  configurations (confirmed with the operator).
- **Assumption:** the shipped baseline should apply identically in dev and
  production/distributed builds, with local `localStorage` overriding locally
  (confirmed with the operator).
- **Risk — stale baseline:** the committed file can drift from current tuning.
  *Mitigation:* document the refresh workflow; keep the file as the single
  source of the shipped baseline (like the CSVs).
- **Risk — surprising local overrides:** a user who previously saved the old
  `Default` values in `localStorage` keeps them locally. *Mitigation:* expected
  and consistent with the CSV/localStorage precedence; documented.
- **Scope creep — automatic sync** of local gym edits back to the repo (a
  dev-mode write path analogous to the CSV plugin) is **out of scope** here and
  should be recorded as a separate work item if wanted.
